land.text: the Electorate of Württemberg (1803-1805), raised to a kingdom

predecessors.note: The Pressburg treaty of 26 December 1805 recognised the royal title.

land.text: the state as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918 (Free People's State of Württemberg)

successors.note: The state was a federal state of the German Empire from 1871 and ended in November 1918 (see the dissolve event); the Weimar Republic took over its land (Free People's State of Württemberg). The German Empire was its overlord, not its successor, so it is no longer listed here (fx-53 D01, was the 1871 dissolve into german-empire; same change as fx-46 R122 for Bavaria); the hierarchy.csv row kingdom-of-wurttemberg -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator.

capitals.name: Stuttgart
capitals.note: The page lists Stuttgart as the only capital.

rulers.name: Frederick I
rulers.note: The infobox gives 1805-1816; he 'assumed the title of King Frederick I on 1 January 1806' and 'died on 30 October 1816'.

rulers.name: Charles I
rulers.note: The reign runs past the map's 1871 end of the state.

keyframe_review.note: 16,895 km2 against the page's 'total area of the state was 19,508 km2' (as defined in 1813): ratio 0.87, inside the factor of two. The electorate's last shape (1805) is 10,032 km2, so the kingdom adds about 6,900 km2 in 1806: the Pressburg page gives Württemberg 'scattered Austrian holdings in Swabia' and the Württemberg page says the king 'greatly extended the borders of the kingdom by the process of mediatisation'. The shape stands for 1806-1810; no cession is on the page.

16,916 km2 (ratio 0.87 to the 19,508 km2 of 1813), identical in cells to 1806 apart from 21 km2. The page records no territorial change between 1810 and 1871 (the Treaty of Paris exchanges of 1810 and the Treaty of Fulda of November 1813 are not on it); the Prussian occupation of the north in 1866 was not a change of owner.
16,915 km2, unchanged; the page's 25 November 1870 military convention put the troops into the XIII Corps of the German Army, and in 1871 Württemberg joined the German Empire.

region.text: the scattered Austrian holdings in Swabia, 'passed to French allies' (the King of Württemberg and the Elector of Baden)

ledger.note: 1806: Austrian Swabia comes to Württemberg. 'The scattered Austrian holdings in Swabia were passed to French allies', among them 'the King of Württemberg' (Pressburg page, treaty of 26 December 1805). The region is the whole 1805-to-1806 growth; the share that came from Austria rather than from the mediatisations is not on the pages.

region.text: the former Electorate of Württemberg with the Austrian holdings and mediatised lands added in 1806

ledger.note: 1806: Württemberg becomes a kingdom. 'Frederick III ... assumed the title of King Frederick I on 1 January 1806' (the infobox dates the elevation 26 December 1806); the Peace of Pressburg of 26 December 1805 had Francis II recognise 'the kingly titles assumed by the Electors of Bavaria and Württemberg'. The page names no boundary.

region.text: former imperial cities, church lands and counts' lands: 'substantially enlarging his territory through the annexation of former imperial cities and church lands'

ledger.note: 1806: the mediatisations enlarge Württemberg. The king 'greatly extended the borders of the kingdom by the process of mediatisation' and 'received further territory with 160,000 inhabitants'. The Confederation page dates the treaty 12 July 1806 (Article 25 legalised the mediatisation of imperial knights and counts); the mediatisation page lists houses mediatised into Württemberg without 1806 dates. Same cells as the Austrian gain above: the split between the two is not on the pages.

1866: Prussia occupies northern Württemberg. 'In 1866, Württemberg took up arms on behalf of Austria in the Austro-Prussian War'; the allies were beaten at Tauberbischofsheim three weeks after Königgrätz (3 July); 'The Prussians occupied northern Württemberg'. Month inferred from the page's sequence; the region is the page's 'northern Württemberg' cut with a 45 km disc around Heilbronn.
1866: peace. The Prussians 'negotiated a peace in August 1866' (the Austro-Prussian War page dates the Peace of Prague 23 August 1866). Withdrawal date not on the page.

region.text: the state's outline as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918

ledger.note: 30 November 1918: the king abdicates. 'King William abdicated on 30 November 1918' (infobox 'German Revolution: 30 November 1918'); 'The kingdom was replaced with the Free People's State of Württemberg'. Infobox status 'Federal State of the German Empire (1871-1918)'. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War

zones.text: northern Württemberg, occupied by the Prussians

wars.outcome: Württemberg fights for Austria, is beaten at Tauberbischofsheim and occupied in the north; peace in August 1866 with no territorial loss.

wars.name: Franco-Prussian War
wars.outcome: A military convention of 25 November 1870 puts Württemberg's troops into the XIII Corps of the Imperial German Army; Württemberg joins the German Empire in 1871. No territorial change.

certainty.note: Treaty and mediatisation borders; the page gives no boundary and Cliopatria's single shape from 1811 is unverified in detail (page budget 1-2: Württemberg, plus the shared Pressburg, mediatisation, Confederation and Austro-Prussian pages). 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

sources.title: Peace of Pressburg (1805)
sources.note: 26 Dec 1805: Bavaria receives Tyrol, Vorarlberg, Augsburg; royal titles; Swabian holdings to Wurttemberg and Baden.

sources.title: German mediatisation
sources.note: Recess of 25 Feb 1803 (Bavaria: Augsburg, Bamberg, Freising, Passau, Wurzburg; Dalberg's Regensburg electorate with Aschaffenburg and Wetzlar); Confederation of the Rhine 1806.

sources.title: Confederation of the Rhine
sources.note: 12 July 1806 founding and member joining dates (Wurzburg 23 Sept, Saxony 11 Dec 1806, Lippe 11 April 1807); dissolved 4 Nov 1813.

sources.title: Austro-Prussian War
sources.note: 15 June 1866 Prussian invasion of Hanover, Saxony and Hesse-Kassel; Peace of Prague 23 Aug 1866; Bavarian losses.

sources.title: Kingdom of Württemberg
sources.note: 1 Jan 1806 royal title; 19,508 km2 (1813); mediatisation gains; 1866 Prussian occupation of northern Wurttemberg; 1871.

sources.title: German Empire
sources.note: Constituent states: the other states retained their own governments; all ruling kings, dukes and princes abdicated in November 1918.

sources.title: German revolution of 1918-1919
sources.note: Abdications: by the end of November 1918 the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated.

notes:
END YEAR: 1871 (German Empire); the monarchy lasted to 30 Nov 1918.
UNSETTLED: the 1806 growth (about 6,900 km2) is split by no page between Austrian Swabia (Pressburg) and the mediatisations; the 1810 Treaty of Paris exchanges with Baden and Bavaria and the November 1813 Treaty of Fulda are not on the Württemberg page (Cliopatria's 1810/1811 change is 21 km2, nothing to explain). Hohenzollern land was never Württemberg's.
CONFLICTS: 1 January 1806 (text) against 26 December 1806 (infobox) for the elevation; Frederick's reign from 1805 (infobox) or 1806; the mediatisation page dates the Confederation 12 June 1806, the Confederation page 12 July.
GAZETTEER: Heilbronn and Ludwigsburg are not gazetteer places; a lon/lat disc is used for northern Württemberg. REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (kingdom-of-wurttemberg_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row kingdom-of-wurttemberg -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator.
